chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said:

A man came to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) from beyond the river of Balkh and said, 'I want to ask you a question; if you answer me in accordance with what I have, I shall affirm your Imamate.' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Ask whatever you wish.'

The man said, 'Inform me about your Lord — when was He, how was He, and upon what was His support?' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, established the «where» without a «where» for Himself, and established the «how» without a «how» for Himself, and His support was upon His own power.'

So the man stood up, kissed his head, and said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that Ali is the legatee of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and the custodian after him with what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) stood for, and that you all are the truthful Imams, and that you are the successor after them.'

key_terms.أَيَّنَ الأَيْنَ: Established/created the 'where' — a profound theological formula stating God originated spatial categories without being subject to them
key_terms.اعْتِمَادُهُ عَلَى قُدْرَتِهِ: His support/reliance upon His own power — God is self-sufficient and self-sustaining
key_terms.الْخَلَفُ: The successor/representative — referring to Imam al-Ridha as the legitimate successor of the preceding Imams
key_terms.كَيَّفَ الكَيْفَ: Established/created the 'how' — God originated modalities of existence without being subject to any modality
key_terms.وَصِيُّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Legatee/successor of the Messenger of Allah — referring to Imam Ali's divinely appointed authority

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about God's existence and whether He has a 'where' or 'how'?
ai.summary: In this hadith, a man from the distant city of Balkh — across the Oxus River in Central Asia — comes to test Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Imam, by posing classical theological questions about God's nature: when did He exist, how did He exist, and upon what does He depend. The Imam's answer masterfully transcends the categories of human knowledge: God Himself created the very notions of 'where' and 'how,' yet is not subject to them; His existence depends on nothing but His own power. The man, satisfied that this answer matches his own understanding of divine transcendence, immediately professes the full Shia creedal formula including the Imamate. This narrative illustrates how the Imams served as authoritative guides to Islamic theology, particularly the doctrine of tanzih (divine transcendence beyond human categories).
